report:
Where things stand: the espresso machine question is partly agreed and partly unresolved. Nothing has been decided about money or arranging, and I made no commitments on anyone's behalf.

CONFIRMED NEEDS (each restated as a noncontroversial essence and checked with the person; recorded only after they said it fit):
• A: "To be able to count on the coffee setup without it costing me time and energy I don't have after long days." Plus two additions A confirmed: "To not be the one who organizes the coffee setup or takes on its upkeep," and "To have a simple, low-upkeep way to make coffee available — kept open, not left to one person's judgment."
• B: "To keep the machine that holds my dad's memory and my own history, working, in the kitchen and in use" (explicitly: not put away somewhere safe). Plus: "To not add counter clutter or extra upkeep," and "To have service arranged without it eating my limited time — it needs to fit small slots."
• C: "To have coffee I can rely on, without having to carry the job of chasing and managing everyone to get there."
• Me: "To know the leak isn't quietly doing damage in the kitchen while we sort out a longer-term answer." Checked with all three; C called it reasonable, A called it a sensible precaution, B accepted it.

AGREED BY A AND B: the old machine gets repaired properly and stays in the kitchen in daily use, with a service/maintenance arrangement so breakdowns don't get chased by any of them. First step: someone checks the leak. (This is A and B's agreement on the substance; it is not a decision I made.)

UNRESOLVED — recorded as unresolved, not settled:
1. Who arranges the service and the "small and low-upkeep" test. C explicitly declined ("that's the chasing I don't want to carry"); A declined ("I can't take on the organizing"); B asked that it not land on her. Nobody has taken it on.
2. Who approves spending. Nobody in the conversation knows. I cannot decide or move money.
3. The exact wording of the "small and low-upkeep" test. B wants it agreed before anything is added and will not accept a machine imposed over her objection; A wants the simple option kept open and not vetoable by one person. I drafted a test (small enough not to clutter the counter, no upkeep from anyone, applied by rule rather than case-by-case) but it was not confirmed by both.

MY OWN STATED VIEW (flagged as a concern, not a decision): the two blocking items — arranging and spending approval — sit with someone outside this conversation. Until that person is named, the repair stalls and the chasing lands on someone by default, which is the outcome C asked to avoid. Both A and B confirmed my final summary as accurate; A agreed someone outside the three needs to be identified, and B asked that the arranging not quietly land on her.

Next step if this continues: identify the person who can approve spending and own the arrangements, and get the test wording confirmed by A and B together.
